about: The calibration table of economy features 3 to 8 (docs/ECONOMY_DESIGN.md): what the port of BeforeIT.jl is given for England in the start year of the world. tools/sim/calibrate_economy.ts computes the port's parameters from it and writes public/data/economy_cities.json: one economy per city of the game, each at its share of England (section cities; feature 5). Amounts are those of the sources (the whole of England); the script scales them.

kinds.source: the number stands in the named source, which was opened on 15 November 2026
kinds.derived: computed from numbers with a source by the stated rule
kinds.assumption: no source was found; the value is a placeholder and no statement about history

scale.source: the diorama scale 1:100 agreed for the game (Ramon, 14 November 2026); the model computes the scaled-down economy

period: the table is yearly (the historical series are annual; the original model computes quarters); the model computes days, see clock

clock.about: Economy feature 4 (docs/ECONOMY_DESIGN.md): one period of the model is one day. src/sim/economy/calibration.ts (dailyEconomy) turns the yearly amounts of this table into daily ones; the rules and their sources are listed there and in the design document.

days_per_year.source: the yearly amounts of the sources are spread evenly over 365 days: the year has no seasons. A leap day of the calendar is computed as a day like any other

plan_days.source: Dawid, Gemkow, Harting, van der Hoog, Neugart (2011), The Eurace@Unibi Model, Model v1.0 User Manual, section 2.3 (a firm acts 'monthly on the ideosyncratic day of the month to act') and section 4.1.1 ('Firms perform the following activities on a monthly base'), opened on 15 November 2026; a month is taken as 30 days

cities.about: Economy feature 5 (docs/ECONOMY_DESIGN.md): every one of the 30 largest cities is an economy of its own, and the cities trade with each other. src/sim/economy/calibration.ts (cityTable) makes the table of a city from this one.

structure.source: none. Every city has the economy of England in 1356 at the city's share of England's people: the same sectors, shares, wages and behaviour. No city has data of its own

duty_shillings_per_sack.source: none. England's wool duty was a duty of the crown on exports out of the realm, not between cities. Between the cities no duty is raised; the crown of a city takes all its revenue as a direct tax

unemployment_benefit.source: no source opened: that none of these cities paid a person without work a benefit in 1356 is general knowledge, not a table. 0 switches the model's benefit off (Poledna et al. 2023, appendix A.44, A.53: a person without an employer is paid theta_UB times the last wage); it is written as a rate of 1e-9 because the port divides the starting wage by this rate (src/agents.rs, line 222). From economy feature 6 to feature 8 the value was 0.55, the constant of the original code's calibration (theta_UB = 0.55 * (1 - tau_INC) * (1 - tau_SIW); BeforeIT.jl, src/utils/calibration.jl, line 549; src/calibration.rs, line 1287 of the port), set for the time being because with the price rule of the paper a slump of a city fed itself when a person without work bought nothing. With wages in money (feature 7) and the demand pull (feature 8) a firm that sells less lowers its price or its supply, and the cities keep their people in work without the benefit (economy feature 9, measured; docs/ECONOMY_DESIGN.md, section 9). Taken out by Ramon's word of 16 November 2026. What a person without wage work lived on (savings, family, church, guild) is not in the model: such a person has no income and buys nothing

wage.source: no source for 1356. In the model of the port a firm has a real wage that never changes and pays it times the consumer price level (BeforeIT.jl, src/agent_actions/firms.jl, lines 120 to 127 and 221; Poledna et al. 2023, appendix A.26), so the wage follows the prices one to one and nothing holds the level of prices. 'money': a firm has a wage in money that never changes, the constant nominal wage of Assenza, Delli Gatti, Grazzini (2015), Emergent Dynamics of a Macroeconomic Agent Based Model with Capital and Credit, CESifo Working Paper 4765, table 2 (w = 1), opened on 16 November 2026. How it enters the port's model is ours, not the papers': every day the real wage of a firm is set to its wage in money over the consumer price level, and in the cost push (A.9) the price of labour is the wage in money instead of the consumer price level (economy/src/clock.rs). A wage that never changes cannot fall either. Trial runs outside the game on 15 and 16 November 2026 (29 cities, 30 and 100 years): with it the price level stays at its start; the rules of the papers that tie the wage to the labour market (Dosi et al. 2015, equation 8; Lengnick 2013, equation 5) did not hold in the cities. 'prices' is the port's wage. Set by Ramon's word of 16 November 2026 (economy feature 7)

prices.source: no source for 1356. 'costs' is the rule of the paper: a firm's supply is the demand it met, and its price moves with its costs and with expected inflation only (Poledna et al. 2023, appendix A.5, A.8, A.9). 'demand': the demand pull of CANVAS: a firm compares the demand it met with the supply it had planned and changes either its supply or its price by the gap between the two (Hommes, He, Poledna, Siqueira, Zhang (2022), CANVAS: A Canadian Behavioral Agent-Based Model, Bank of Canada Staff Working Paper 2022-51, section 3.2.4, equations 34 to 37, opened on 15 November 2026; BeforeIT.jl, src/model_extensions/init_CANVAS.jl, lines 45 to 75; src/model_extensions/canvas.rs of the port). What is ours: a firm applies it on its plan day every 30 days, with the mean demand per day since its last plan, where CANVAS applies it every quarter (economy/src/clock.rs); and every planning firm adjusts (theta_calvo = 1, the default of the original code). The central bank that learns its rule, the other change of CANVAS in the original code, is not taken. Trial runs outside the game on 15 and 16 November 2026 (29 cities, 30 and 100 years): with the port's wage this rule drove prices to zero within 7 to 11 years; on top of the wage in money (cities.wage) it held. Set by Ramon's word of 16 November 2026 (economy feature 8)

gdp_nominal_gbp_mn.source: Bank of England, A millennium of macroeconomic data, version 3.1, sheet A1, column V, year 1356: nominal GDP at market prices (Broadberry, Campbell, Klein, Overton, van Leeuwen)

population_thousand.source: same workbook, sheet A1, column Z, year 1356

value_added_share.source: Broadberry, Campbell, van Leeuwen (2013), When did Britain industrialise?, Explorations in Economic History 50(1), table 7A, year 1381 (the first year with a documented structure; the authors use the weights of 1381 for 1270 to 1450)

participation.source: same paper, pp. 13-14: rates of the nineteenth century, carried back by the authors

income_gbp_mn.source: Clark, England NNI (workbook of 2015), sheet Decadal, row 1350-59. Only the shares of income are used: Clark's level is about twice Broadberry's

interest.source: Clark, Microbes and Markets, table 7, p. 34: return on rent charges in the 1340s (one transfer). The table has no observation for the 1350s; the next one is 5 % in the 1370s. Footnote 15, p. 32 (Thrupp, Bean): returns of 6 to 8 % in the middle of the fourteenth century

crown_revenue_gbp_thousand.source: Bank of England workbook, sheet A26, column C, year 1356: tax revenue, nine-year moving average (O'Brien and Hunt)

coin_gbp_mn.source: same workbook, sheet A22, column C, year 1356: coin in circulation (Palma)

wool_export.source: Munro (2011), Statistical tables on medieval and early-modern textiles, table 1 (sacks, mean of 1356-60) and table 14 (denizen price and duty per sack, 1356-60)

cloth_value_gbp.source: Munro (2011), table 8, gives no value of a cloth before 1371; this is its value for 1371-75. Cloth is about a tenth of the exports of 1356-60

output_per_intermediate_input.source: none. The earliest input-output table for England is that of 1841 (Horrell, Humphries, Weale 1994), not read (paywall)

input_matrix.source: none (see above). Column = buying sector, row = supplying sector, each column sums to 1

persons_per_firm.source: none. A social table of around 1290 exists (Campbell 2008, p. 940), not read (paywall)

adult_share.source: none read: share of the people aged 15 and over (the poll tax of 1377 would be the source)

unemployed.source: none: the smallest number the port accepts

unemployment_benefit.source: England had no unemployment benefit in 1356 (common knowledge, no table). 0 switches the model's benefit off (switched_off). The cities take the value of section cities, which is 0 as well since economy feature 9

depreciation.source: none: share of the capital stock used up in a year

import_share.source: none: what is imported, and imports are set as high as exports. An import series exists only from 1560

investment_share.source: none: what firms buy to invest

dwelling_share.source: none: what households buy to build

bank_equity_of_coin.source: none: equity of the model's one bank as a share of the coin

rest_of_the_world.source: none: output and inflation abroad stay constant

behaviour.source: the values of the original model, estimated on today's banks and firms (Poledna et al. 2023; src/calibration.rs of the port): repayment rate, capital requirement, loan-to-value limit, capital buffer, capacity utilisation at the start. The sizes of firms follow the power law of the original

derived.value_added: GDP at market prices minus the wool duty (the one tax on products of the model), split by the shares of the sectors
derived.capital_stock: capital income other than house rents, divided by the interest rate
derived.dwellings: house rents divided by the interest rate
derived.crown_spending: the crown spends its revenue (a spending series exists only from 1688)
derived.direct_tax: crown revenue minus the wool duty
derived.household_consumption: what is left of the supply of each sector after inputs, crown, investment, dwellings and exports
derived.land_rent: has no place of its own in the model: it is part of the profit of the firms
derived.labour_force: people x adult share x mean participation of men and women; one person in persons_per_firm is the owner of a firm
derived.crown_and_export_shocks: AR(1) on the logarithm of the series below, 1281 to 1356, by the port's formula (estimate_for_calibration_script)

switched_off.about: Institutions of the model that England did not have in 1356. They are parameters of the port, set so that they do nothing.
switched_off.taxes: value added tax, social insurance of firms and workers, corporate tax, taxes on investment, on government purchases, on products and on production: 0
switched_off.unemployment_benefit: England's own table: off (inputs.unemployment_benefit = 0), written as a rate of 1e-9 instead of 0 because the port divides the starting wage by this rate (src/agents.rs, line 222). The cities of the game have it switched off as well (cities.unemployment_benefit = 0, economy feature 9); from feature 6 to feature 8 they paid 55 % of the last wage after tax
switched_off.pensions_and_benefits: 0; the model's one inactive person stands for the minimum the port needs
switched_off.central_bank: policy rate fixed at 0 (rho = 1, no Taylor rule); the loan rate is the interest rate above
switched_off.shocks: covariance of the shocks: exports as estimated, 1e-12 for output abroad and imports (the port needs a positive definite matrix)

history.about: The years before the start. The firms of the model form their expectations from the output of all earlier years (appendix A.6, A.7), so the model needs the real history.
history.source: Bank of England, A millennium of macroeconomic data, version 3.1: sheet A1 (real GDP at market prices and its deflator, Broadberry et al.; export volume) and sheet A26 (tax revenue, O'Brien and Hunt). Single values, not the workbook, which carries no open licence
